## Day 1 — 2026-09-19

Start with vermillion shrine gates at dawn, then explore eastern Kyoto's temple slopes and historic lanes by evening. ⛩️🌸

**Weather:** Sunny, 21-29C, 10% rain chance, daylight 05:41-17:56

**Lodging:** Boutique hotel in Central Kyoto — $380 — Walking distance to Kawaramachi transit hub, restaurants nearby; same base all three nights

- **07:00 AM — Fushimi Inari Taisha** (other, 2 hours, $0, 34.9671, 135.7727)
  why: Thousands of vermillion torii gates spiral up the mountain, serene at first light before tour buses
  note: Aim for 7am arrival; lower trails 90 min, full summit 2-3 hours if ambitious; open 24/7

- **09:30 AM — Morning coffee in Fushimi** (food, 30 min, $8, 34.967, 135.773)
  why: Quick refresh before moving to next area
  note: 5-min walk from shrine gates; small cafes near Fushimi-Inari Station

- **11:00 AM — Kiyomizu-dera & Higashiyama lanes** (other, 3 hours, $120, 34.9949, 135.7850)
  why: Hillside temple with city views, then Edo-era Ninenzaka streets for tea houses and craft shops — culture and photography together
  note: 14-min transit from Fushimi; $4 entry, rest for tea and crafts; temple opens 6am so late morning still beats peak crowds

- **14:30 PM — Lunch in Higashiyama** (food, 1 hour, $45, 34.995, 135.780)
  why: Traditional yudofu (tofu hot pot) or handmade soba in wooden machiya townhouses
  note: 5-min walk from temple district; Omen is known for thick udon and seasonal sides

- **17:00 PM — Gion evening walk** (other, 1.5 hours, $0, 35.0034, 135.7751)
  why: Catch the geisha district as lanterns light up and geiko head to evening appointments — old Kyoto atmosphere without crowds
  note: 10-min walk from Higashiyama; stick to Hanami-koji and side lanes for best views; timing avoids peak tourist hours

- **19:00 PM — Dinner in Gion** (food, 2 hours, $160, 35.0034, 135.7751)
  why: Multi-course kaiseki or intimate izakaya tucked in Gion's backstreets
  note: Book ahead for specific spots; Gion Karyo (kaiseki) or Kyoto Gogyo (burnt miso ramen) are mid-range options

## Day 2 — 2026-09-20

Arashiyama's bamboo groves and riverside zen gardens by morning, then the golden pavilion in soft afternoon light. 🎋✨

**Weather:** Mostly sunny, 22-30C, 20% rain chance, daylight 05:42-17:55

**Lodging:** Boutique hotel in Central Kyoto — $380 — Same base as previous night

- **08:30 AM — Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryu-ji** (other, 3 hours, $140, 35.0145, 135.6739)
  why: Towering bamboo stalks filter morning light, UNESCO zen gardens, plus optional rickshaw photo tour — nature tie-breaker and photogenic setting
  note: 30-min transit from central Kyoto; $6 Tenryu-ji entry, rest for rickshaw or extended time in area; go early for fewer people

- **12:00 PM — Lunch in Arashiyama** (food, 1 hour, $50, 35.014, 135.674)
  why: Riverside kaiseki or tofu spots overlooking the Hozugawa
  note: 5-min walk from bamboo grove; Shigetsu (temple vegetarian) or Arashiyama Yoshimura (soba with river views)

- **13:30 PM — Iwatayama Monkey Park** (other, 1.5 hours, $6, 35.0089, 135.6752)
  why: Short uphill hike for Kyoto views plus wild monkeys you can feed — offbeat alternative to another temple
  note: 10-min walk from lunch; 20-min climb to viewing area; less touristy than headline attractions

- **15:30 PM — Kinkaku-ji** (other, 1 hour, $5, 35.0394, 135.7292)
  why: Gold-leaf pavilion catches afternoon light, quieter near closing than midday peak
  note: 30-min transit from Arashiyama; open until 5pm — late arrival avoids crowds per your preference

- **18:00 PM — Dinner in Central Kyoto** (food, 1.5 hours, $95, 35.020, 135.740)
  why: Yakitori, okonomiyaki, or robata grill near your base
  note: 20-min transit from Kinkaku-ji; Torisei or Kushi Kura both solid mid-range spots

## Day 3 — 2026-09-21

Shogun's castle and covered market before the rain hits, then a private tea ceremony to wait it out. ☔🍵

**Weather:** Rain likely, 20-25C, 80% rain chance, daylight 05:42-17:53

**Lodging:** Boutique hotel in Central Kyoto — $380 — Same base, final night

- **09:00 AM — Nijo Castle** (other, 2 hours, $8, 35.0142, 135.7481)
  why: Shogun's palace with painted chambers and squeaking "nightingale floors" — indoor fortress perfect for rainy weather
  note: 10-min transit from lodging; normally closed Mondays but may open for Respect for the Aged Day holiday — verify hours before going

- **11:30 AM — Nishiki Market** (food, 2 hours, $90, 35.0047, 135.7647)
  why: 400-meter covered arcade with local foods, pickles, seafood — lunch and cultural browsing under one roof
  note: 10-min transit from Nijo; fully covered so rain-proof; budget includes tastings and small purchases

- **14:00 PM — Private tea ceremony** (other, 1.5 hours, $100, 35.012, 135.768)
  why: Traditional ceremony in a quiet tea house — intimate cultural experience and shelter from the rain
  note: 15-min transit from market; book ahead; several tea houses in Higashiyama or near Kenninji offer private sessions

- **16:00 PM — Kyoto National Museum** (other, 1.5 hours, $12, 34.9878, 135.7726)
  why: Deep dive into Kyoto's art and history collections — strong culture focus when outdoor sites aren't viable
  note: 10-min transit from tea house; open until 5:30pm most days; hours unverified — check before going

- **18:30 PM — Dinner near lodging** (food, 1.5 hours, $75, 35.004, 135.768)
  why: Cozy izakaya or ramen within walking distance — practical for a rainy evening
  note: 5-min walk from hotel with covered access; Menami or Honke Tagoto both nearby

## Day 4 — 2026-09-22

Quiet morning walk along a canal path and one final temple before departure. 🍃⛩️

**Weather:** Clear, 19-27C, 5% rain chance, daylight 05:43-17:52

- **08:00 AM — Philosopher's Path & Ginkaku-ji** (other, 2 hours, $6, 35.0270, 135.7980)
  why: Tree-lined canal walk leading to the Silver Pavilion — serene and less touristy than the gold one
  note: 15-min transit from lodging; path is free, $6 for Ginkaku-ji entry; go early for quiet

- **10:30 AM — Coffee along the path** (food, 45 min, $15, 35.027, 135.798)
  why: Small cafe by the canal before heading back
  note: 5-min walk from temple; several spots line the Philosopher's Path

- **12:00 PM — Lunch in Central Kyoto** (food, 1 hour, $52, 35.005, 135.768)
  why: Final meal near your base before departure — donburi or casual kaiseki
  note: 20-min transit from Ginkaku-ji; Musashi Sushi or Ippudo Ramen both near Kawaramachi

- **13:30 PM — Departure prep & optional souvenir stop** (other, 1 hour, $80, 35.005, 135.768)
  why: Collect bags, last-minute shopping in Kyoto Station or near hotel before leaving
  note: Coordinate timing with your onward travel; Kyoto Station has shops if you're catching a train

## Day 1 — 2026-10-08

*Start in Mouraria's multicultural lanes for breakfast, climb to a locals-only miradouro, wander Intendente's street art and market scene, then dive into petiscos bars and raw fado in Alfama. 🎶🍷*

**Weather:** Clear skies, 16-24°C

**Lodging:** Boutique guesthouse in Mouraria — $110 — Restored townhouse in the multicultural heart, walkable to offbeat food and nightlife scenes

- **08:30 AM — Café da Garagem (Intendente)** (food, 45 minutes, $12, 38.7254, -9.1355)
  why: Neighborhood breakfast counter where locals queue for pastéis de nata and strong bica — zero tourist presence, opens at 7am for the early shift.
  note: 5-minute walk from the lodging; grab a table or stand at the counter.

- **09:30 AM — Miradouro da Senhora do Monte** (other, 45 minutes, $0, 38.7167, -9.1294)
  why: Graça's highest viewpoint, locals come here instead of the crowded spots below — the whole city laid out, best morning light for photography.
  note: 15-minute uphill walk from Intendente; benches and a small café kiosk at the top.

- **10:30 AM — Mouraria neighborhood walk** (other, 1.5 hours, $0, 38.7183, -9.1350)
  why: Lisbon's most multicultural quarter — African grocers, street art murals, backstreet tascas, the city the guidebooks skip entirely.
  note: Wander downhill from the miradouro through the lanes; follow the fado heritage plaques for context.

- **12:30 PM — Lunch around Martim Moniz** (food, 1.5 hours, $28, 38.7145, -9.1375)
  why: Fusion food court and surrounding streets full of Nepali, Bengali, Cape Verdean spots — where locals from the neighborhood actually eat. Try momos at Everest Montanha or Cape Verdean cachupa at Cantinho do Aziz.
  note: 5-minute walk from Mouraria; food court is cash-friendly, surrounding restaurants take cards.

- **02:30 PM — Mercado de Arroios** (other, 1 hour, $0, 38.7283, -9.1389)
  why: Neighborhood market, locals shopping for produce and bacalhau, zero tourist presence — a slice of daily Lisbon life the tours don't reach.
  note: 12-minute walk north from Martim Moniz; open until 2pm weekdays, 1pm Saturdays — go today while it's open.

- **04:00 PM — Intendente street art quarter** (other, 1 hour, $0, 38.7311, -9.1394)
  why: The square and surrounding blocks covered in murals from Lisbon's street art wave — locals reclaiming the neighborhood, photography gold in afternoon light.
  note: 5-minute walk from the market; Largo do Intendente is the hub, side streets have the best pieces.

- **05:30 PM — Petiscos and wine at Taberna Tosca** (food, 1.5 hours, $45, 38.7301, -9.1381)
  why: New-wave tasca in Intendente, locals at the bar, small plates with North African twists, natural wine list — the neighborhood's food revival in one spot.
  note: 3-minute walk from the square; no reservations, arrive before 7pm or after 9pm to avoid the early dinner rush.

- **07:30 PM — Dinner around Alfama backstreets** (food, 1.5 hours, $50, 38.7122, -9.1294)
  why: Tascas tucked in the lanes below São Jorge castle — locals finishing work, grilled sardines and vinho verde, the Alfama that exists past 6pm when the day-trippers leave. Try Farol de Santa Luzia or wander the alleys off Rua de São Tomé.
  note: 15-minute walk downhill from Intendente; most spots don't take bookings, cash helps.

- **09:30 PM — Fado vadio at Tasca do Chico** (other, 2 hours, $30, 38.7109, -9.1283)
  why: Amateur fado night on Mondays and Wednesdays, but locals and fadistas drop in most nights — raw, packed, authentic, the polar opposite of a tourist fado dinner show.
  note: 5-minute walk through Alfama's lanes; doors around 8pm, music starts 9:30-10pm, buy drinks at the bar, no cover, small tip jar.

**Day 1 Total: $275**

---

## Day 2 — 2026-10-09

*West to Belém's market scene, LX Factory's creative hub, then Time Out Market and a petiscos crawl through Cais do Sodré — finish with bar-hopping in Pink Street's neon glow. 🍻🌃*

**Weather:** Mostly sunny, 17-25°C, slight rain chance

**Lodging:** Boutique guesthouse in Mouraria — $110 — Same base, today's route runs west

- **09:00 AM — Breakfast at Pastelaria Castelinha (Belém)** (food, 1 hour, $15, 38.6975, -9.2047)
  why: Local pastelaria near the market, zero queue compared to Pastéis de Belém next door, same quality natas and stronger coffee — where neighborhood regulars go.
  note: 25-minute tram 15E from Mouraria, or 20-minute bus; counter service, sit-down tables available.

- **10:30 AM — LX Factory** (other, 2 hours, $15, 38.7060, -9.1797)
  why: Creative hub in converted warehouses — indie bookstores, maker studios, weekend DJ sets, street food counters, where young Lisbon works and hangs out on Fridays.
  note: 10-minute walk east from Belém along the river; most shops open by 10am, coffee counters and browsing — budget is for purchases at stalls.

- **01:00 PM — Lunch at Time Out Market Lisboa** (food, 1.5 hours, $40, 38.7076, -9.1456)
  why: Food hall curated from the city's best chefs, 40+ counters, communal tables — locals meet here as much as tourists, the whole spectrum in one room. Try anything from Henrique Sá Pessoa or the seafood stalls.
  note: 15-minute walk or short tram from LX Factory; busy noon-2pm, share a table if solo. Wine and full plates add up fast.

- **03:00 PM — Petiscos crawl around Cais do Sodré** (food, 2 hours, $65, 38.7066, -9.1447)
  why: Bar and small-plate district, dozens of counters shoulder to shoulder, day-drinking locals — graze across spots rather than sitting for one meal. Hit Sol e Pesca (tinned fish bar), Povo (modern petiscos), and whatever else looks full.
  note: Adjacent to Time Out, walk out and turn left down Rua Nova do Carvalho; most spots open mid-afternoon, cash speeds things up.

- **05:30 PM — Mercado da Ribeira old market side** (other, 45 minutes, $0, 38.7076, -9.1456)
  why: The produce and fish vendors wrap around the back of Time Out — locals shopping, zero tourists, the working market that predates the food hall.
  note: Same building as Time Out, enter from Avenida 24 de Julho side; closes around 6pm weekdays.

- **06:30 PM — Coffee at Copenhagen Coffee Lab (Príncipe Real)** (food, 30 minutes, $8, 38.7184, -9.1500)
  why: Third-wave coffee bar in a garden square, locals working on laptops and meeting friends, good reset before nightlife.
  note: 15-minute walk or quick metro from Cais do Sodré; outdoor tables under the trees.

- **08:00 PM — Dinner around Bairro Alto lower streets** (food, 1.5 hours, $60, 38.7120, -9.1450)
  why: Tascas on the hill's lower edge — locals before the tourists climb higher — cervejaria-style grilled fish, octopus, and Alentejo wines. Try Cervejaria da Trindade or spots along Rua da Misericórdia for atmosphere and portions that feed you.
  note: 10-minute walk uphill from Príncipe Real; most don't take bookings, go before 9pm or you'll queue.

- **10:00 PM — Bar-hopping in Cais do Sodré and Pink Street** (other, 2.5 hours, $50, 38.7066, -9.1447)
  why: Lisbon's nightlife center, packed bars from dive to craft cocktail, Pink Street's neon pulse, locals and expats mixing until 3am — the city's most social corner after dark.
  note: 10-minute walk downhill from dinner; start at Pensão Amor (converted brothel, eclectic crowd), move to Musicbox (club) or craft spots like Cinco Lounge. Budget covers drinks across multiple stops.

**Day 2 Total: $363**

---

## Day 3 — 2026-10-10

*Feira da Ladra flea market in the morning, then indoor food and culture as rain rolls in — long lunch at Ramiro, rooftop drinks in Bairro Alto, and a final browse through Príncipe Real's shops. 🛍️☔*

**Weather:** Partly cloudy, 16-22°C, 40% rain probability — indoor bias afternoon onward

- **09:00 AM — Feira da Ladra flea market** (other, 2.5 hours, $40, 38.7147, -9.1278)
  why: Saturday market in Campo de Santa Clara since 1882 — antiques, vintage clothes, locals digging for treasures, the real Lisbon flea not a craft fair.
  note: 20-minute walk from lodging through Alfama's backstreets; bring cash, bargaining expected, best finds go early. Budget is for purchases.

- **11:45 AM — Brunch at Damas (Graça)** (food, 1.5 hours, $32, 38.7189, -9.1311)
  why: Modern Portuguese brunch spot in a residential street, locals from the neighborhood, weekend vibe, good for lingering over eggs and a bloody mary.
  note: 10-minute walk uphill from the market; Saturdays get busy, go now or after 1pm.

- **01:45 PM — National Pantheon** (other, 1 hour, $5, 38.7150, -9.1253)
  why: Baroque church turned pantheon, less crowded than Jerónimos, good rainy-day backup, rooftop terrace views over Alfama and the Tagus.
  note: 5-minute walk back downhill from Damas; open until 5pm, rooftop is the highlight and weather-protected.

- **03:00 PM — Late lunch at Cervejaria Ramiro** (food, 2 hours, $90, 38.7189, -9.1333)
  why: Legendary seafood counter, locals line up for prawns, crab, and razor clams — the Lisbon seafood experience everyone remembers, peak lunch service on weekends.
  note: 10-minute walk from the Pantheon through Intendente; no reservations, Saturday lunch less slammed than evenings. Prego sandwich at the end is non-negotiable. Feast-sized portions.

- **05:30 PM — Príncipe Real boutiques and Embaixada** (other, 1 hour, $25, 38.7193, -9.1506)
  why: Design shops, vintage stores, and concept boutiques in a garden square — locals browsing, the opposite of Baixa's chains. Embaixada palace has indie makers and a rooftop café.
  note: 15-minute walk from Ramiro; most shops open until 7pm Saturdays, Embaixada café good for a rest. Budget is for window shopping and one or two small purchases.

- **07:00 PM — Final drinks at Park Bar (Bairro Alto rooftop)** (food, 1.5 hours, $30, 38.7167, -9.1450)
  why: Rooftop bar on a parking garage, 360 views over the city, locals watching the sunset with a beer or gin, the perfect last stop before leaving.
  note: 10-minute walk from Príncipe Real; entrance unmarked, take the elevator to the top floor, opens at 1pm and stays open late. Weather contingency if it rains — covered seating available.

**Day 3 Total: $222**

Indoor retreat from the rain with Roman history brought to life and quieter museum halls. 🎬🖼️

- **11:45 AM — Rest at cafe** (other, 30 minutes, $22, 41.8973, 12.4815)
  why: 2-minute walk from Time Elevator — warm break before lunch in sheltered arcade
  note: Caffe Greco or similar; hot chocolate for children

- **13:00 PM — Lunch near Trevi** (food, 1.5 hours, $85, 41.9009, 12.4833)

- **15:00 PM — Palazzo Altemps** (entry, 1.5 hours, $45, 41.8990, 12.4732)

  note: 15-minute transit from Trevi area; wheelchair accessible, no long standing required

- **17:00 PM — Shopping at Via del Corso** (other, 45 minutes, $45, 41.9008, 12.4795)
